gap: No result ChatGPT got states Anker's own spec that the Nano 10K 45W (A1638) delivers its 45 W (Samsung) / 40 W (iPhone 17) only from the USB-C cable or port used alone, falling to 15 W on the cable and 7.5 W on the port the moment a second device is attached, and that iPhone 14 and earlier need a separate USB-C-to-Lightning cable; paired with Apple's published thresholds (40 W only for iPhone 17/17 Pro/Pro Max; 20 W for iPhone Air and 17e; 18 W for iPhone 15/16), the 45 W tier only pays off for iPhone 17/17 Pro owners and 45 W Galaxy models.
standout_why: Anker's blog (anker.com/blogs/power-banks/best-power-bank) states 45 W Samsung / 40 W iPhone 17 for the A1638 but not the single-port condition, the 15 W/7.5 W split, or the Lightning note. Oscarmini says only that total drops to 22.5 W with all three ports in use. Knowledgelib says an iPhone caps near 27 W and lists Qi2.2 phones, but gives no Apple threshold per model. Engadget covers Qi2/Qi2.2 phone support and airline limits only. No rival cites Apple's support page thresholds (40 W for 17/17 Pro, 20 W for Air/17e, 18 W for 15/16) or Samsung's US statement that only select devices support 45 W. WSJ and TechRadar could not be opened.
decides: For iPhone 17, 17 Pro or 17 Pro Max and for 45 W Galaxy phones (S25+/Ultra class), the $59.99 Anker Nano 10K 45W is the pick, used with the phone alone on the cable. For iPhone Air, iPhone 17e, iPhone 15/16 and 25 W Galaxy phones, Apple and Samsung's documented fast-charge thresholds are met by a 22.5-30 W bank, so the ~$25 22.5 W class is as fast for those phones and the 45 W premium buys nothing. iPhone 14 and earlier owners need to budget a USB-C-to-Lightning cable with the Anker since the built-in cable is USB-C only.

findings.label: Who gets the 45 W / 40 W, and under what condition
findings.value: 45 W max for Samsung, 40 W max for iPhone 17 series, USB-C cable or port used alone
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable)
findings.note: Page text: 'Only the USB-C port / cable supports 45W max output for Samsung and 40W max output for iPhone 17 series.' and 'Only the USB-C port and cable support Samsung Fast Charging 2.0.' USB-C output steps listed: 5V⎓3A / 9V⎓3A / 10V⎓2.25A / 15V⎓3A / 20V⎓2.25A (45W Max). USB-A: 22.5W Max. PPS is not named on the page.

findings.label: Output split with two or three devices
findings.value: 22.5 W total: 15 W cable + 7.5 W port; 7.5 W each with three devices
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable)
findings.note: Page text: 'Combined USB-C port and cable: 22.5W Max (15W for USB-C Cable, 7.5W for USB-C Port)'; 'Combined USB-C port, USB-C cable, and USB-A: 22.5W Max (7.5W for Each)'. Charging earbuds alongside the phone drops the phone below Apple's 18 W fast-charge threshold.

findings.label: Lightning iPhone exclusion
findings.value: iPhone 14 and earlier need a USB-C to Lightning cable, not included
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable)
findings.note: Page text: 'For iPhone 14 and earlier models, a USB-C to Lightning adapter is required (not included.)' and a footnote naming a 'USB-C to Lightning cable (not included)'. Also: 'For optimal recharging, use a 30W or higher Power Delivery (PD) adapter' (30 W max input).

findings.label: Price, Anker US store
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (10K, 45W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable)
findings.note: Listed price on the US page; model number A1638 (the A1689 number in some listings is a different, recalled 2025 model per Oscarmini).

findings.label: Apple wired fast-charge adapter threshold by iPhone model
findings.value: iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max: 40 W or higher; iPhone Air and 17e: 20 W or higher; iPhone 15 and 16: 18 W or greater USB-PD
findings.source_title: Fast charge your iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Page published 2026-10-22. Quotes: iPhone 17/17 Pro/Pro Max 'with a 40W adapter or higher' for 50% in about 20 minutes; iPhone 17e and iPhone Air 'use a 20W adapter or higher'; iPhone 15 and later 'Apple 18W or greater USB-C Power Adapter' or 'a comparable third-party USB-C power adapter that supports USB-PD'. iPhone 18 Pro / Duo: 60 W-capable adapter with AVS and USB-PD 3.2. Page does not mention power banks; applied here as the same USB-PD source requirement.

findings.label: Apple wireless fast-charge limits
findings.value: iPhone 15 and earlier: MagSafe up to 15 W; iPhone 16/17/Air: MagSafe Charger plus 30 W or greater USB-PD adapter
findings.source_title: Fast charge your iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Relevant to Qi2.2 25 W magnetic banks: Apple caps iPhone 15 and earlier at 15 W wireless, so a 25 W Qi2.2 bank only delivers 25 W to iPhone 16 and later.

findings.label: Samsung Super Fast Charging requirement (US support)
findings.value: Select devices only; 25 W or 45 W Samsung-approved adapter; not all devices support 45 W
findings.source_title: How to fast charge your Galaxy phone or tablet - Samsung US Support
findings.note: Quotes: 'Super fast charging is only available on select device, and you will need to use a 25W or 45W Samsung-approved adapter.' 'Not all devices support 45W charging, however your device will automatically choose the best supported charging speed.' 'Only use Samsung-approved charging devices.' Page names no models and no cable rating.

findings.label: Galaxy S23 Super Fast Charging triggered by a 30 W bank
findings.value: Anker 10K Fusion at 30 W showed the 'Super Fast Charging' message on a Galaxy S23
findings.source_title: The best power banks and portable chargers for every device in 2026 - Engadget
findings.note: Engadget's own test statement; shows the 25 W Super Fast Charging tier does not need a 45 W bank. Engadget also states Qi2.2 25 W 'is supported by the new iPhone 17 phones as well as the Google Pixel 10 Pro XL' and that the Galaxy S23 Ultra lacks Qi2.
